objective: Replace compose's in-form AttachmentPicker panel with a stats picker modal: the attach row's bar chart opens a second Dialog over the composer holding the stats navigator in select mode (Seasons and Players, down to a game's final score, a played box-score line or a career scope), with Cancel and a Select that stays disabled until a selectable row is chosen; and close the thread's carried risks R22 (a Dialog's initial focus), R23 (a failed lazy chunk breaks the app until a reload), R25 (the picker's share of the navigator chunk), R29 (one ok() helper in api/), R30 (Back before a cold record's list lands) and R32 (cold-chunk findBy warm-ups).
acceptance_criteria: The bar chart (ChartColumnIcon, accessible name "Attach stats", at least 44 px square, a visible focus ring) opens the picker: UI-010's Dialog (components/ui/Dialog) titled "Attach stats", opened over the compose Dialog (one inside the other, as a ConfirmDialog opens inside the thread modal), with aria-haspopup="dialog" on the button and no aria-expanded or aria-controls. A reply address still offers no bar chart, and InlineComposer (the thread's reply box) still offers none. AttachmentPicker's panel, its three choice buttons and its native selects are gone; what is attached is still summarised under the attach row with "Remove attached stats", whether the picker has ever been opened or not, and a pre-filled /compose?link= address is still checked and attached on arrival with the same notes and the same words as today (prefilled-link.test.tsx may change only for the bar chart's new attributes, each change named in the PR).

The picker holds a SegmentedTabs bar Seasons / Players (the human, 2026-10-26: no Records tab, because a record is never attachable) over the shared StatsNavigator (components/stats-nav/) in its state-driven form: the stack is the picker's own state, no address changes while the picker is open, and every level control is a button (the adapter gives no levelHref). The Seasons tab carries the season select (SeasonSelect) above the navigator, as on the Stats page, opening on the newest season, conference All; picking a season starts the stack afresh at that season. SeasonSelect takes its id from useId, so the picker's select and the Stats page's under it never share an id and each is named "Season". The picker starts afresh each time it opens (Seasons, the newest season, the root level, nothing chosen).

Levels: Seasons → season (standings, the All / East / West bar, a team row opens the team level) → team (its record and its games, newest first; a game row opens that game's level) → game (the human, 2026-10-26: the game's level holds both game types): a "Final score" row first, then the box score's played lines (player, team, minutes, points, rebounds, assists), home side first, as playedLines orders them; and Players → the search (UI-010's SearchInput, at least 2 letters, debounced as today, the API's order, paged as on the Stats page's Players tab, through the shared PlayerResults) → player (the player's name as the heading, then a Regular season row and a Playoffs row with games played and career points). StatsLevel grows by {kind:"game",gameId}, {kind:"players"} and {kind:"player",playerId} in components/stats-nav/types.ts only, and every use narrows by kind. StatsNavigator draws the season and team levels itself and takes every other level's breadcrumb name and view from its caller (a LevelViews prop: name(level) and view(level, {open, replace}), whose open moves focus as the navigator's own controls do): RecordsTab passes the records views, and the picker passes its game, players and player views, which live in features/compose/ (the picker's chunk), because stats-nav may import nothing under features/ but features/games/format and the selection rules and summary words stay in features/compose/attachmentReads.ts. TeamLevel takes an optional onGame(gameId), which the navigator passes in select mode, so a game row is a LevelLink button opening the game level with the navigator's focus rule; on the Stats page it is undefined and the row still links to /games/<id>. The breadcrumb, Back and the focus rule are the navigator's. On the Stats page nothing visible changes: the Players tab still links to /players/<id>, and the records levels behave as before (but for R30).

Selectable rows, and nothing else (the three data_link types, and the rules attachmentReads.ts applies today): a game's Final score when the game is completed (not both scores 0), a played line (seconds_played not null; a did-not-play line is not offered), and a career scope with games_played above 0. A row that is not selectable (an unplayed game's Final score, a scope with no games) is shown as plain text, never as a disabled control. A selectable row is a native radio input labelled with the row's words, in one radio group per level named by that level's heading, so a row is chosen by click, Space or the arrow keys; one choice is held across the whole picker (choosing another replaces it, and moving between levels keeps it), and one polite status line above the buttons names it ("Selected: <its summary>") or says "Nothing selected".

Cancel and Select: a footer under the navigator with Cancel (secondary) and Select (primary), Select disabled (the Button primitive's disabled state) until a selectable row is chosen. Select sends link-attached with that link to the mediator (which replaces any link already attached, as today), remembers its summary (describeGame / describeLine / describeCareer, so the summary under the attach row and Undo read as today), and closes the picker. Cancel, Escape and the backdrop close the picker and attach nothing. Escape in the picker closes only the picker, never the composer under it; however the picker closes, focus returns to the bar chart (the Dialog's own rule), and the draft's text, image and link are as they were. Enter inside the picker never submits the draft: the picker's Dialog is rendered outside the compose <form> (or its content sits in a <form> of its own whose submit is prevented), and a test pins that Enter in the search box and Enter on a radio send no POST /posts (the skeptic measured both posting the draft in a prototype that nested the dialog in the form).

R18: nothing inside the picker leaves it. Every game, team and player in the picker opens a level or is a radio, never a link to another page, so the picker never starts or continues a modal flow; a test pins that the picker renders no <a href> at all.

Reads (R29 and the brief's design note): the picker reads through src/api/ only, with the Stats page's query keys and staleTime (a team, a season or a game opened on Stats is not asked for again in the picker within its staleTime, and the other way round). api/stats.ts gains seasonsQuery() with SEASON_STALE_TIME (SEASONS_KEY is read today with the client default), and the game detail and player detail reads (fetchGameDetail, fetchPlayerDetail and their query options), typed from api/schema.d.ts, with features/games' and features/players' keys and shape exactly: ["events","games",id] holding GameDetailOut | null and ["events","players",id] holding PlayerDetailOut | null (null on a 404), so one key never holds two shapes; features/games/ and features/players/ keep their own reads unchanged. attachmentReads.ts defines no fetcher: its address check calls api/stats.ts's fetchGameDetail and fetchPlayerDetail, the reads the picker's game and player levels use, and it keeps the selection rules and the summary words. So compose imports api/stats.ts statically, which Rollup puts in its own stats chunk loaded with the composer: a read module, not navigator code. api/stats.ts and api/records.ts share one ok() helper in src/api/ok.ts instead of a private copy each.

Lazy and light (R25, R1): the picker is its own lazy chunk, imported when the bar chart is first pressed, never when compose opens, and waited for inside the picker's Dialog behind a loading line, never the composer's or the page's Suspense; opening compose fetches no picker or navigator code. No records view (RecordsLevel, RecordLevel, recordLabels, api/records.ts) is in any chunk the picker loads: by the LevelViews injection above they are in RecordsTab's chunk only. lazy-routes.test.ts and stats-nav-lazy.test.ts pin what the entry, the compose chunk and the picker chunk may not import statically.

R23: a lazy chunk that fails to load is not cached as failed (on origin/main a failed compose chunk replaces the whole app with React Router's "Unexpected Application Error"). When the composer's chunk (routes/ComposeModal.tsx's loadComposer) or the picker's chunk fails, the dialog shows an InlineAlert in place of its content ("We could not open this just now. Please try again.") with a Try again button; Try again, or closing and opening again, imports the chunk afresh: no React.lazy (it caches its rejection per lazy()), a module-level promise cleared on rejection; and because Vite's preload helper never requests a stylesheet twice, Try again first replaces every same-origin stylesheet link that failed (in Chrome its sheet is non-null but reading cssRules throws, or it has none), so the recovered content is styled. A success then shows the content with no reload. The browser row checks a computed style (the picker footer's position: sticky) after recovering.

R22: a Dialog's initial focus is its Close button, set by Dialog itself after showModal() whatever the browser chose, unless a child moves it in its own effect (the thread's reply box and a confirm's Cancel keep doing so). The compose page's text box takes autoFocus (the human, 2026-10-26: R38), so compose opens with focus in the text box; the picker opens with focus on its Close. In Chrome, closing compose that was opened from inside the detail modal puts focus on the detail's Close (FRONTEND-020 criterion 2, the browser row it missed; on origin/main it lands on the Dialog's content scroller).

R30: Back and the breadcrumb's first item on a record level always return to that record's own group, also when pressed on a cold /stats/records?record=<id> before its list lands (Back from a cold ?record=player-points-game lands on ?group=player with Player selected, at any moment); until the list or the cached summary names the group, it is the record id's own prefix (team- or player-, every EVENTS-010 id in 0x02's registry), and an id with neither keeps today's behaviour; the breadcrumb and the records level's heading never name the wrong group meanwhile. It costs no request.

R32: every test file that reaches a lazy stats tab through the route table (StatsPage.test.tsx and routes/routes.test.tsx among them) warms its lazy chunks in a beforeAll, as d30f892 did for four files, so a first findBy never races a cold import under the full suite's load; no assertion changes.

Accessibility: the picker's tab bar is SegmentedTabs (tablist, arrow keys, one tab stop); the picker's Dialog is anchored at the top, as ComposeModal.module.css anchors compose, so it grows downward as levels land; every table keeps its caption, column scopes and row headers; every radio has a visible focus ring and a label naming the row; the status line is announced politely; at 360 wide nothing in the picker moves sideways but a table inside its ScrollTable, and the footer stays on screen (position: sticky); nothing prints null, undefined or NaN.

Every existing frontend test passes, except a test that pins AttachmentPicker's panel, its choice buttons and selects, the bar chart's aria-expanded, the compose dialog's initial focus, a lazy() Suspense in the compose Dialog, the record level's breadcrumb before its list lands, or the navigator's level union; such a test is changed or replaced in the test commit and named in the PR body. The skeptic's prototype broke these (47 tests in 6 files), each changed in the test commit since test edits are frozen during implementation: AttachmentPicker.test.tsx (25: criteria 1-5 and 12 move to the picker's tests), ComposePage.test.tsx (15: criteria 6 and 7, which attach through the panel), attach-row.test.tsx (2: the disclosure checks), compose-style.test.tsx (3), RecordLevel.test.tsx ("reads Records in the breadcrumb until the list lands", which pins R30's old behaviour) and lazy-routes.test.ts ("puts a Suspense inside the compose Dialog", R23); component-isolation.test.ts changes only if AttachmentPicker.tsx is renamed or deleted. Any Director correction of a test is its own commit, before the implementation commit, named in the PR.
